claim: Let \(n\ge 2\). For each \(r\in[1,\infty]\), let \(p_r=\|\cdot\|_r\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Then \(p_r\) and \(p_s\) lie in the same intrinsic part of \(\mathcal N(\mathbb R^n)\) if and only if \(r=s\). For \(1<r<\infty\), the separating local triangular-defect asymptotic along \(e_1\) and \(e_1+t e_2\) is \(\Delta_{p_r}(e_1,e_1+t e_2)=((1-2^{1-r})/r)t^r+O(t^{2r})\). Consequently, for every \(n\ge 2\), the cone of equivalent norms on \(\mathbb R^n\) has continuum many intrinsic parts.

correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the source criterion and checks all parameter regimes. For \(1<p<q<\infty\), the explicit expansion has positive coefficient \(c_r=(1-2^{1-r})/r\) and makes the defect ratio tend to zero. The two nonsmooth endpoints are separated by explicit differences in defect zero sets. The restriction from \(\mathbb R^n\) to the first two coordinates is exact.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the canonical \(\ell^r\) family under a newly introduced intrinsic-part invariant. It strengthens a single published separation example to continuum many pairwise distinct parts in every real dimension at least \(2\), and isolates local defect order as a reusable mechanism rather than merely recomputing one parameter pair.
